text:
sasha: Heads up — since ~09:10 UTC we're seeing a sharp spike in streaming token deadline misses from us-west1 GPU pool. Dashboard shows RPC deadline_exceeded alerts and lots of out-of-order packet indicators at the same time.

mike: Can you paste a few log lines?

sasha: sure. snippet from the model-proxy logs around 09:12:
```
rpc_id=stream-5f0c model=gpt-medium node=gpu-12 rpc_deadline_ms=200 stream_tokens_ms=120 out_of_order=1 retransmits=3
rpc_id=stream-5f1a model=gpt-small node=gpu-22 rpc_deadline_ms=200 stream_tokens_ms=80 out_of_order=0 retransmits=0
```
Also kernel dmesg on gpu-12 shows a burst of scattering/skipped packets and GRO warnings.

infra-bot: Alert: stream_deadline_exceeded (count: 73 in 10m) tagged us-west1-gpupool.

anya: Might be network-level reordering rather than application. Did we change ToR or LAG config recently? ECMP or hash policy could split packets of same connection across paths.

sasha: Not that I'm aware of on our end — no recent infra deploys. But we did flip MTU to 9000 on a subset of hosts last week to reduce CPU overhead.

tori: jumbo MTU + LAG/ECMP can definitely surface as reordering if some paths still use 1500 or LSO/GRO behavior is inconsistent. Are these flows RDMA/RoCE or plain TCP?

mike: Some of the fast-path streaming uses RoCE for large model KV transfers between shards, but token streaming itself is normal TCP gRPC from runtime -> model-proxy. However, if RDMA is present on the same NICs, offloads and driver interaction can affect packet ordering.

anya: Quick checks to run on an impacted node (gpu-12):
```
# check NIC offloads and counters
etstat -s | egrep "reordered|out-of-order|retransmits"
etstat -s | tail -n 20
ethtool -k eth0
ethtool -S eth0 | egrep "rx_dropped|tx_dropped|rx_no_buf|rx_missed"
# check link hashing and bonding
cat /proc/net/bonding/bond0 || ip -d link show bond0
# show ECMP routes
ip route show table all | grep -E "nexthop|scope link"
```

sasha: ran a couple: bond0 is on LACP active-backup? actually it's balance-xor on some hosts. ethtool shows GRO: on, GSO: on, TSO: on. counters show rx_missed spikes during incidents.

tori: balance-xor means hashing across different slaves; if switch hashing differs for flows, packets of same 5-tuple might be split across physical paths -> reordering. Also GRO/LRO can coalesce then hand back OOO packets to stack if hardware offload inconsistently applied.

mike: vendor switches sometimes change hashing when flows are large or when MTU mismatches. Can we check ToR logs? @network-team, any recent change in hash seed or flow-table evictions?

oncall-ops: I don't see config changes in our change log. But we had a flapping link on ToR-03 at 08:57 that bounced a transit session for ~30s. Could be related. Vendor name: Broadcom Tomahawk / MLAG.

anya: That lines up. MLAG + flapping trunk + asymmetry = reordering. Short term workaround: disable GRO/LRO/GSO on egress for the runtime interface and force single-path (make bond mode active-backup or set consistent hash) for the GPU-pool VLAN. Doable via chef/ansible?

sasha: I can patch a hotfix to the node profile:
```
# disable offloads to reduce OOO
sudo ethtool -K eth0 gro off gso off tso off
sudo sysctl -w net.core.netdev_max_backlog=5000
```
Rolling that to a subset now. Will monitor.

tori: Another option is to pin NVMe/RoCE QPs to dedicated ports so RDMA traffic doesn't interact with TCP flow paths. Also consider forcing LACP hashing to src-mac/dst-mac only to keep flows on same link.

mike: For RoCE, if ECMP is enabled in the network, packets can be routed differently at layer3. Recommend disabling ECMP for the GPU pod vlans or tweak switch to do per-flow hashing based on the full 5-tuple.

sasha: After disabling GRO/GSO on three affected nodes, the deadline-exceeded alerts dropped by ~70% in the last 8 minutes. Streaming latencies look stable.

oncall-ops: Good catch. We should still open a vendor ticket for the flapping ToR and ask them to confirm MLAG hashing behavior and whether certain firmware releases changed hash seeds.

anya: Agreed. Action items:
- oncall-ops: open support case with switch vendor, attach packet captures and flapping times (assigned)
- infra: roll hotfix (disable GSO/GRO) to all us-west1 GPU nodes as interim (sasha)
- network: check MLAG/LAG hashing and consider forcing deterministic per-flow hashing or single path for GPU VLANs (tori)
- infra: schedule a maintenance window to revert MTU experiment and test 9000 vs 1500 path consistency (mike)

mike: Also add a short-term metric: out_of_order_count by node and flow_id and alert when > 5 in 1m so we catch early.

sasha: filing a follow-up doc in /docs/ops/networking/ with the checks and commands we used. will paste the ticket number once vendor responds. thanks all :thumbsup:

infra-bot: Created incident CR-2026-45, assigned oncall-ops.

tori: If vendor confirms it's MLAG resharding we may need to adjust our traffic engineering — longer term we should consider dedicated leafs for GPU traffic or make GPU pods flow-stick via SRv6 or ECMP pinning.

sasha: For now the hotfix keeps latency stable. I'll update if anything changes.
